benchmarkComparisons: measured this turn on 24 single-file JS fixtures (14 positive, 10 negative) before -> after: positives found 12 -> 13 of 14, false positives 5 -> 0 of 10 (sibling literal field, overwritten field, other array index, other Map key, spread-then-override); the one missed positive is a closure returned from a factory; 35 tests in the new file pass; regression: test:dataflow 1461 pass, mutation 217/217, layer-recall equal to baseline, cve-replay 220/220, self-scan no drift, full npm test 10647 pass 1 fail (dataflow-watch-1, a timing test that passes alone)

benchmarkComparisons: measured this turn on 12 request-to-sink Express fixtures: found 5 -> 11 of 12 (the awaited helper, expression-bodied arrows, promise .then, user callbacks and same-file middleware fields were all missed before); the safe sibling of each is silent; a real IR defect was found and fixed: expression-bodied arrow functions recorded no return, so every helper written as x => expr was invisible to return-taint; regression: test:dataflow 1461 pass, mutation 217/217, layer-recall equal to baseline, cve-replay 220/220, self-scan no drift
knownLimitations: JavaScript/TypeScript with Express-style handlers only; Flask/Django/Spring/Rails propagation is not modelled here
Promise.all destructuring and EventEmitter emit/on hand-offs are not followed (asserted as gaps)

a callback is tainted only for the receiver-value methods and for project functions that call their own parameter

layer-recall corpus has no async or callback entries so it could not show the gain

benchmarkComparisons: measured this turn on 10 call-context fixtures: 7 of 10 correct before, 10 of 10 after. The defect found: a callee's findings were re-merged into its caller on every evaluation, so a chain of N one-line wrappers carried 2^N copies of one finding (131072 at 17 levels) and the finding was lost: chains deeper than 16 and diamonds deeper than 10 were silent; now linear chains of 300 and diamonds of 24 levels find exactly one finding in under 100 ms; regression gates: test:dataflow 1461 pass, mutation 217/217, layer-recall equal to baseline, cve-replay 220/220, self-scan no drift, scan-health 24 pass
knownLimitations: budget exhaustion is reported for five reasons (summary budget, deadline, function limit, callback limit, a thrown analysis); other early exits inside the pre-passes are not yet instrumented
an incomplete analysis is now a scanHealth condition, which makes the scan report degraded; strict CI will treat a hit budget as degraded
k=1 value-context sensitivity with a cap of 16 contexts per function is unchanged; call-string sensitivity stays opt-in
the layer-recall corpus has no deep call chains so it could not show the gain

benchmarkComparisons: measured this turn: 9 language fixtures x 6 dimensions: 17 of 54 cells detected after a fix (11 before): JavaScript and TypeScript detect all 6 dimensions, Flask detects entry point, authentication and role but not ownership, tenant or the sensitive operation, FastAPI and PHP detect only the entry point, Java/Go/C#/Ruby detect nothing; workflow-state-check and transaction-integrity are absent (no deterministic extractor); no control was reported on any unguarded route. A real DCI defect found and fixed by the audit: a one-line handler is its own declaration line, so its sensitive operation and owner scope were skipped; context-intelligence suite 70 pass
knownLimitations: one small fixture per language; not-detected is a statement about this extractor and fixture, not the framework
detected means the extractor reported the kind, not that the control is effective
no accuracy was measured; that is E4-06
the capability matrix was updated: PHP is experimental (entry point only), the others stay unsupported
FastAPI dependencies defined in the same file are not resolved (partially_resolved), a gap recorded, not fixed here

not yet wired into the context command or into findings; that is E4-07

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured on real apps: 7 fixture scenarios: a 3-route order resource (owner-scoped GET, unscoped PUT and DELETE) yields 2 idor inconsistencies naming the enforcing route; a tenant-scoped read beside an unscoped list yields 1 cross-tenant; a service-layer check counts for its route; consistent routes, different resources and a single route yield none; a documented public route is suppressed with its policy id and an expired policy no longer suppresses
knownLimitations: an inconsistency is evidence that a route is weaker than its sibling, not proof of a vulnerability; E4-04 must supply a counterexample
resource names come from the text of the data operation; operations whose target cannot be named are counted and left out
JavaScript/TypeScript and Python only, as the DCI build supports
a bare parameter named user is not treated as the principal (existing precision rule); currentUser, req.user and similar are
write/read/update/delete are told apart by the operation's text, not by a model of the ORM

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured on real apps: on an Express fixture an executed local request showed a non-owner modifying another user's note (proven) while the same attacker got 404 from the owner-scoped sibling; the same candidate is plausible without execution, refuted when the control is on the path or the attempt is denied, unresolved when the fixture cannot run. A real defect found by the injection test and fixed: an inline comment on a code line (/* ownerId: req.user.id */) was read as an ownership control, hiding a real finding; comments and docstrings are now blanked before fact extraction (positions preserved). context-intelligence suite 78 pass
knownLimitations: the fixture runner supports Express-style apps with an in-memory db and the fixture's own relative modules only; anything else ends as unresolved, not proven

confinement is Node's permission model (no file, process or worker access) plus a driver that removes fetch and refuses every builtin and package; network is not part of the permission model, so network is blocked by the driver, which is lower assurance than an OS sandbox
the proof shows an attacker reading or changing a victim's object through the real handler; it does not show the same in the deployed system
comment blanking is a tokenizer, not a parser: unusual literals (regex containing //) could be mis-tokenized
the harness fixture (store, principals, request) is authored by the caller; nothing generates it

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured: behaviour tests with fakes; with the network made to fail, buildContext, invariants, cross-route and a proven counterexample all complete with zero network attempts; a throwing egress check and an unapproved remote endpoint each send zero requests; command-stripping removes 3 of 3 planted commands and leaves prose; anonymized prompts contained no real path while citations still verified; the token cap stopped the run after the first job
knownLimitations: command stripping is a pattern list for shell-looking text, not a proof that no unsafe text remains; nothing executes model text, this protects the people and tools that copy from reports
anonymization replaces file paths only; identifiers inside source code are not renamed, and the existing redaction still handles secrets and PII
a cached review from an earlier non-anonymized run is reused as is (nothing is sent), so the anonymize flag does not retroactively change a cache hit
token counts are estimates (4 characters per token), as elsewhere
the origin/main 0.172.1 DCI hardening was merged into this branch during this task; two small conflicts (config, reachability imports) were resolved by hand
